title: NUS launches S$50M National Centre for Engineering Biology to accelerate AI-guided sustainable biomanufacturing
key_facts: NUS says the National Centre for Engineering Biology (NCEB), hosted at NUS, was officially launched with its new research facility; Desmond Lee, Minister for Education and Minister-in-Charge of Social Services Integration, was guest of honour.

The centre was set up with Nanyang Technological University, Singapore Institute of Technology, Temasek Polytechnic, Nanyang Polytechnic and the Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR), through a National Research Foundation Mid-sized Grant of close to S$50 million over seven years from 2023.

It aims to build knowledge and technology in engineering biology for the sustainable making of specialty chemicals (high-value products and materials) and to move the field from trial and error toward predictive design, in three thrusts: machine learning for predictive biodesign, engineering biology for specialty chemical production, and advanced biofoundry capabilities.

The NUS-led flagship project uses AI-guided engineering biology for sustainable specialty chemicals, with functional fatty acids as first targets; AI platforms propose improved enzyme and pathway designs, which the Advanced BioFoundry (a highly automated facility) builds and tests in large numbers, and results are fed back to improve the next round.

Many specialty chemicals are hard to make by conventional chemistry and rely on energy-intensive, fossil-derived processes; the project aims to make them with engineered microbes and enzymes from renewable feedstocks.
A Bioprocessing Innovation Platform with the Singapore Institute of Technology offers pilot-scale fermentation and downstream processing to carry lab results toward industrial production.
More than 150 researchers, students and staff work on it across the partner institutions, with recruitment ongoing for about 50 more.
The launch marks the start of the first Singapore Engineering Biology Week, 5 to 8 Oct 2026, with about 300 participants; the release lists goals, not results.
quote_evidence: The national-level centre will build foundational knowledge and technologies in engineering biology for the sustainable biomanufacturing of specialty chemicals, an important class of high-value products and materials.

Supported by the National Research Foundation (NRF) under the Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2025 (RIE2025) plan, the Centre was established through the NRF Mid-sized Grant of close to S$50 million awarded over seven years from 2023.

AI-synthetic biology platforms developed at NCEB propose improved enzyme and pathway designs, which the Advanced BioFoundry – a highly automated research facility at NUS – builds and tests in large numbers rather than one at a time.
why_it_matters_hint: A national AI-and-automated-lab centre aims to design microbes and enzymes that make specialty chemicals more sustainably, but it has only just opened and the release gives goals, not results.
event_date: Launched 5 Oct 2026 (release says 'today' and ties the launch to the opening of Engineering Biology Week on 5 Oct).
notes: Read in full. NUS's own news release; the S$50 million is the 2023 National Research Foundation grant, not new money. The release's 'ecosystem' and 'digital backbone' wording is left out of the entry.
